Point Reyes National National Seashore.hint: Features 71,000+ acres of rugged coastline, beaches, and trails; camping is backcountry-only (no car camping).

Muir Woods National Monument.hint: Protected old-growth coast redwoods; parking reservations are required for all visitors.

Golden Gate National Recreational Area.hint: Offers diverse landscapes including coastal prairies, historic military sites, and beaches; entry to the GGNRA is free, though specific attractions or parking may have fees.

Angel Island State Park.hint: Located in San Francisco Bay, accessible by ferry, featuring historic sites and 360-degree bay views.

China Camp State Park.hint: Offers shrimping village history, marshes, and technical multi-use trails.

Mt. Tamalpias State Park.hint: 6,300 acre park, known for redwood groves, oak woodlands, and over 60 miles of trails.

Olompali State Historic Park.hint: Preserves Coast Miwok indigenous history and Spanish-era adobe ruins.

Samuel P. Taylor State Park.hint: A popular 2,780-acre park with redwood groves, Lagunitas Creek, and camping.

Tomales Bay State Park.hint: A remote coastal park featuring Heart's Desire Beach, Shell Beach, and waterfront recreation.

Alto Bowl Preserve.hint: This scenic, grassy hillside is famous for its resident grazing horses and sweeping views of the bay.

Bald Hill Preserve.hint: This steep, prominent peak features open grasslands and essential watershed protection.

Baltimore Canyon Preserve.hint: Visitors flock to this lush, shaded canyon to hike alongside a seasonal creek and view a beautiful seasonal waterfall.

Blithedale Summit Preserve.hint: Dominated by dense redwood groves and steep chaparral, this ridge provides a crucial wildlife corridor to higher mountain peaks.

Bolinas Lagoon Preserve.hint: This vital tidal estuary serves as a major stopover point for thousands of migrating birds on the Pacific Flyway.

Bothin Marsh Preserve.hint: A paved multi-use trail runs right through this tidal wetland, offering excellent opportunities for birdwatching and cycling.

Camino Alto Preserve.hint: Characterized by mixed evergreen forests and steep canyons, this preserve is a popular spot for shaded hikes and mountain biking.

Cascade Canyon Preserve.hint: A serene, densely forested valley centered around a beautiful waterfall and a pristine, rocky creek.

Deer Island Preserve.hint: Once a true island in a larger tidal bay, this isolated, oak-studded hill is now surrounded by diked pastureland and seasonal wetlands.

French Ranch Preserve.hint: A peaceful landscape of rolling, oak-studded hills nestled in a quiet, sunny valley.

Gary Giacomini Preserve.hint: Situated on a high coastal ridge, this unique area harbors rare serpentine soils and a specialized dwarf forest.

Horse Hill Preserve.hint: As its name suggests, this iconic, grassy community pasture is home to grazing horses and offers beautiful open-space views.

Ignacio Valley Preserve.hint: A mix of dense oak woodlands and steep ridges characterizes this tucked-away natural space.

Indian Tree Preserve.hint: Hikers climb through quiet oak woodlands to reach a stunning summit grove of old-growth redwood trees.

Indian Valley Preserve.hint: Shaded, gently rolling trails weave through a bowl-shaped oak forest featuring a seasonal creek and small waterfalls.

King Mountain Preserve.hint: A steep, densely forested knoll traversed by a scenic loop trail that winds through ferns and redwoods.

Little Mountain Preserve.hint: Serving as an ecological transition zone, this lower slope area features a blend of open grasslands and oak woodlands.

Loma Alta Preserve.hint: A challenging climb to one of the region's highest grassy peaks rewards hikers with spectacular 360-degree views.

Loma Verde Preserve.hint: Quiet, neighborhood-accessible trails wind through the steep, oak- and bay-forested canyons of this tranquil preserve.

Lucas Valley Preserve.hint: A prominent, grassy ridgeline dominated by a massive landmark boulder offers sweeping panoramic views of the surrounding area.

Maurice Thorner Preserve.hint: This compact sanctuary protects a vital ridge covered in dense chaparral and native oaks.

Mount Burdell Preserve.hint: Known for exceptional spring wildflower blooms, this massive, rocky mountain features hidden ponds and sweeping vistas.

Old Saint Hilary's Preserve.hint: A steep, windswept hillside famous for its spectacular springtime display of incredibly rare, endemic wildflowers.

Pacheco Valle Preserve.hint: Trails in this deep, shaded canyon follow a peaceful creek through dense stands of bay and oak trees.

Ring Mountain Preserve.hint: Renowned for its unique geology, this prominent ridge harbors rare plants found nowhere else on earth.

Roy's Redwoods Preserve.hint: An open, sunny meadow is entirely encircled by towering, majestic old-growth redwood trees.

Rush Creek Preserve.hint: Blue oak woodlands stretch alongside vital seasonal wetlands, creating a haven for hundreds of species of waterfowl.

San Pedro Mountain Preserve.hint: A prominent, chaparral-covered ridge physically divides the bay ecosystem from the inland valleys.

Santa Margarita Island Preserve.hint: A small, oak-canopied hill surrounded by marshland becomes temporarily stranded by water during heavy winter rains.

Santa Venetia Marsh.hint: This small but critical tidal marsh serves as a vital high-tide refuge for endangered native marsh birds.

Terra Linda / Sleepy Hollow Preserve.hint: A long, rolling grassy divide offers miles of sunny ridge-walking and expansive views.

Tiburon Ridge Preserve.hint: This high, narrow ridge provides a crucial trail link and breathtaking views of the bay and nearby straits.

Verissimo Hills Preserve.hint: A rugged landscape of steep, grassy slopes dotted with mature oak trees.

White Hill Preserve.hint: A steep, prominent forested crossing acts as a bridge between two major coastal watersheds.

Adrian Rosal Park.hint: A small, sunny neighborhood gathering space offering a half-basketball court, play structures, and a grassy lawn.

Agate Beach Park.hint: A rocky coastal shoreline famous for its extensive tide pools teeming with marine life during low tide.

Aramburu Island.hint: A restored shoreline sanctuary in the bay providing critical habitat and isolation for harbor seals and migratory shorebirds.

Bayside Park.hint: A peaceful waterfront area providing picnic spots and gentle walking paths right along the edge of the bay.

Black Point Boat Launch.hint: A convenient, paved ramp providing boaters and kayakers direct access to the tidal waters of the nearby river.

Bolinas Park.hint: A quaint, grassy downtown gathering space featuring shade trees, a playground, and public restrooms near the coast.

Buck's Landing.hint: A scenic waterfront access point historically used for brick-making, now serving as a peaceful spot for launching kayaks into the bay.

Candy's Park.hint: A beloved, heavily shaded neighborhood pocket park offering a cozy playground under a canopy of mature redwood trees.

Castro Park.hint: A lively community recreation area featuring a basketball court, play equipment, and mature shade trees for neighborhood families.

Charles F. McGlashan Pathway.hint: A paved, multi-use path traversing beautiful coastal wetlands, popular with local cyclists and birdwatchers alike.

Chicken Ranch Beach.hint: A warm, sandy, family-friendly shoreline nestled along a sheltered bay, perfect for swimming and launching paddleboards.

Corte Madera Pathway.hint: A smooth, flat multi-use trail following an old railroad right-of-way directly alongside vital tidal marshlands.

Forest Knolls Park.hint: A deeply shaded community play area tucked away under a towering canopy of mature evergreen trees.

Hal Brown Park.hint: A sprawling, family-friendly area boasting expansive turf, a healing garden, and stunning views of the region's most iconic mountain peak.

Lagoon Park.hint: A tranquil recreation space featuring a calm, enclosed body of water popular for shoreline fishing and model boat sailing.

Lagunitas Skate Park.hint: A compact, rural action-sports facility offering local youth a concrete bowl and street features tucked into a forested valley.

Lucas Valley Park.hint: A sunny, open community space featuring rolling turf, a playground, and picnic areas surrounded by golden, grassy ridges.

McInnis Park.hint: A massive recreation hub offering everything from a nine-hole golf course and tennis courts to batting cages and wetland trails.

McInnis Skatepark.hint: A dynamic, large-scale concrete complex designed for action sports enthusiasts with a variety of bowls, rails, and ramps.

McNears Beach Park.hint: A beautifully landscaped shoreline destination offering a fishing pier, tennis courts, a swimming pool, and a sandy beach along the bay.

Mill Valley / Sausalito Pathway.hint: This highly popular, paved recreational trail skirts the edge of the bay, providing stunning water views and a flat route for commuters and walkers.

Miller Boat Launch.hint: A major regional boating facility offering multiple launch ramps and a long pier extending out into a sprawling, sheltered bay.

Paradise Beach Park.hint: A beautifully landscaped, terraced recreation area featuring a fishing pier, colorful gardens, and a calm beachfront nestled along the bay.

Point Reyes Playground.hint: A charming, community-built play structure situated in a small coastal town, providing a perfect resting spot for families exploring the coast.

Pueblo Park.hint: A simple, welcoming neighborhood green space offering a playground and an open lawn for local residents.

San Geronimo Park.hint: A rural community gathering spot nestled in a forested valley, featuring play structures and quiet picnic areas.

Stafford Lake Bike Park.hint: An exhilarating, multi-level dirt track facility designed specifically to challenge mountain bikers and BMX riders of all skill levels.

Stafford Lake Park.hint: A sprawling, scenic destination surrounding a peaceful reservoir, renowned for its extensive disc golf course and large lakeside picnic areas.

Tiburon Uplands.hint: A densely wooded, steep hillside trail system offering hikers a cool, shaded canopy and occasional glimpses of the bay below.

Upton Beach.hint: A quiet, sandy stretch of ocean shoreline perfect for peaceful walks and dramatic surf watching, located just north of a larger, more crowded state beach.

Village Green Park.hint: A classic, manicured central plaza featuring a lovely gazebo and grassy lawns tailored for community events and quiet lunches.

Whitehouse Pool.hint: A popular, scenic access area situated at the edge of a coastal stream, providing an excellent launching point for kayakers heading toward the bay.

Miwok Park.hint: Dog friendly and has a Native American museum

Hamilton Wetlands.hint: Wetlands nature preserve featuring walking/cycling trails, plus egrets & other wildlife.

Marin French Cheese Company.hint: Cheese-themed picnic venue by a pond.

Lawson's Landing.hint: Venerable fishing & boating resort, established in 1929, with a family-owned tent/RV campground.

Cypress Tree Tunnel.hint: Drive planted in around 1930 with Monterey cypress trees, leading to a historic radio station.
